subject: civil-engineering
intro: Civil engineering plans and builds the built world — bridges, water systems, roads and foundations — leading to work designing structures, taming floods, moving traffic and teaching the craft.

roles.title: Civil Engineers
roles.what: Perform engineering duties in planning, designing and overseeing the construction and maintenance of structures and facilities such as roads, bridges, dams, pipelines and water and sewage systems.
roles.where: Structural analysis and design, geotechnical engineering, hydraulics and hydrology map directly onto facility design duties, and the construction-and-economics unit covers the estimating side.

roles.title: Transportation Engineers
roles.what: Develop plans for surface transportation projects to engineering standards and public policy, prepare designs, specifications and estimates, and modify streets and highways to improve traffic flow.
roles.where: The transportation-engineering unit — highway geometry, pavement design, traffic flow and capacity — plus engineering economics give you the estimating and design basis of the job.

roles.title: Environmental Engineers
roles.what: Prevent, control and remediate environmental hazards using engineering: waste treatment, site remediation and pollution-control technology, protecting water, air and land.
roles.where: The environmental-engineering unit's water and wastewater treatment, air-quality and solid-waste topics are the hazards this role is hired to engineer away, with hydraulics behind the plant design.

roles.title: Surveyors
roles.what: Make exact measurements and determine property boundaries, providing data on the shape, location, elevation and dimension of land and land features for engineering, mapmaking and construction.
roles.where: The geotechnical unit's soil characterisation and the highway geometry of the transportation unit are built on survey data, making this course's measurement discipline directly usable in the field.

roles.title: Civil Engineering Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Apply theory and principles of civil engineering to help plan, design and oversee construction and maintenance of structures and facilities, working under the direction of engineering staff.
roles.where: Mechanics of materials, soil classification, the rainfall–runoff process and the estimating topics of the construction unit are the calculations technicians run on real projects every day.
